narrative: The PR rebuilt the commit lock on flock. Most later findings trace to fixes that handled one instance of a class and left its siblings. The F1 ctx fix covered only the contention return, which led to the F6 entry gate. That gate made the F1 test vacuous (F7/F16/F19/F21) and left the blocking-I/O window, which the agent first pushed back on (F14) and then conceded (F22/F28). The F4 durable-record fix covered snapshots new only, so restore and store mutations came back as eight duplicate threads, and the rewritten restore closure still dropped the rotated path on install failure (F24/F27/F29). The F25 condemned-shape fix used a sign-tolerant ParseInt and left the artifact arm's label unchecked (F30/F32/F34), and the F23 budget resize left stale '~30s' comments (F31/F37). Every round also carried at least one finding no fix caused, so no round is strictly avoidable, but most of rounds 2-4 is fix-caused.
guidance_observations: The isUserSnapshotName reconcile bug was reported in the round-0 and round-1 review summaries (round 1 called it blocking) but was only fixed after it came back as two inline threads in round 2; summary-body findings need the same response as inline ones.

Fix commits repeatedly scoped to the reviewer's named instance (one caller, one return path, one predicate arm) instead of the shared wrapper or the whole class, which produced clusters of 3-4 duplicate findings in the next round.

The agent deferred one pre-existing bug to a ticket (F15) while fixing another equally pre-existing one in the same round (F17), then reversed the deferral a round later; one explicit in-PR-vs-ticket rule (does it ship in this release?) would have saved the F25 thread.
Fixes that added an early gate or changed a constant were not followed by a check of the tests and comments downstream of them (vacuous tests after the entry gate, stale ~30s after the resize).
